subtitle: Four Historians, One Uprising, Many Wars Over Memory

panels.shot: epic split-screen tableau, each historian at a desk with 1857 scenes swirling faintly behind them
panels.action: Archive Quartet of 1857 sits as four distinct figures in different eras, each surrounded by papers and faint ghostly images of sepoys, princes and peasants rising in 1857.

dialogue.text: One revolt. Four historians. From mutiny to war of independence to subaltern rebellion, 1857 keeps changing—because its tellers keep fighting over what it was.

i18n.hi: एक विद्रोह, चार नज़रिए। ग़दर, आज़ादी की जंग, मज़दूरों की बग़ावत—१८५७ बदलता रहता है, क्योंकि उसके किस्सागो लड़ते रहते हैं कि वो था क्या।

panels.shot: slow push-in on a dusty shelf of colonial records, with Kaye’s figure emerging from the shadow
panels.action: Archive Quartet of 1857 figure in Victorian dress runs a gloved hand along leather-bound volumes labelled ‘1857’ on a high shelf, London fog against the window.

dialogue.text: The first great story of 1857 was written in London, not Lucknow. It rose from dust-covered dispatches, private letters and official fears bound into imperial history.

i18n.hi: १८५७ की पहली बड़ी कहानी लंदन में लिखी गई, लखनऊ में नहीं। धूल भरे संदेशों, निजी ख़तों और हुकूमती ख़ौफ़ों से एक साम्राज्य की तारीख़ घड़ी गई।

panels.shot: medium shot of Kaye at his desk, lamplight on his face, Indian maps spread before him
panels.action: Victorian Kaye of the Archive Quartet sits at a heavy desk, pen poised, Indian maps and court-martial reports spread out, a small bust of Queen Victoria watching.

dialogue.text: John William Kaye called it the ‘Sepoy War’. Drawing on officers’ reports and Company files, he saw a soldier mutiny that spread into a crisis of empire.

i18n.hi: जॉन विलियम के ने इसे ‘सिपाही युद्ध’ कहा। अफ़सरों की रिपोर्टों और कंपनी के काग़ज़ों से उसे एक सिपाही बग़ावत दिखी, जो जल्दी ही साम्राज्य का संकट बनी।

panels.shot: low-angle view over Kaye’s shoulder, showing his manuscript page where ‘mutiny’ is underlined
panels.action: From behind Kaye, we see his inked manuscript page where the word ‘mutiny’ is sharply underlined, while outside the window regimental drills unfold on a parade ground.

dialogue.text: Kaye and G.B. Malleson named it ‘the Indian Mutiny’. Princes became ‘intriguers’, villagers ‘rabble’, rebel proclamations ‘fanatic’. Their words fixed British memory for generations.

i18n.hi: के और जी.बी. मैलिसन ने इसे ‘इंडियन म्यूटिनी’ कहा। राजे बन गए ‘साज़िशी’, गाँववाले ‘भीड़’, बाग़ी एलान ‘धर्मांध’। उनकी ज़बान ने पीढ़ियों के लिए ब्रिटिश याद तय कर दी।

panels.shot: wide shot juxtaposing Kaye at desk and, in ghostly overlay, Indian rebels marching
panels.action: Kaye writes steadily while translucent images of sepoys, talukdars and townsfolk march and gather above him, their faces serious, unseen by the man at the desk.

dialogue.text: Kaye’s archive was rich but one-sided. Rebel voices came filtered through trial records and officers’ notes. The uprising spoke, but in a language its enemies recorded.

i18n.hi: के का ख़ज़ाना भरपूर था, पर एक तरफ़ा। बाग़ियों की आवाज़ें आईं तो मुक़दमे की फ़ाइलों और अफ़सरों के नोटों की छाननी से। उठाव बोल रहा था, पर दुश्मनों की लिखी ज़बान में।

panels.shot: swift transition shot: pages of Kaye’s book dissolve into a spinning chakra and Savarkar appears
panels.action: Kaye’s printed pages whirl like a storm; they dissolve into a spinning chakra motif as Savarkar’s figure from the Archive Quartet steps forward, holding a worn Marathi pamphlet.

dialogue.text: Half a century later, another voice rose in London. Vinayak Damodar Savarkar read the same mutiny and renamed it ‘The Indian War of Independence’.

i18n.hi: आधे सदी बाद, लंदन में एक और आवाज़ उठी। विनायक दामोदर सावरकर ने उसी म्यूटिनी को पढ़ा और नाम दिया ‘इंडियन वॉर ऑफ़ इंडिपेन्डेन्स’।

panels.shot: close-up on Savarkar’s intense face as he annotates British accounts
panels.action: Savarkar leans over British histories with a pencil, circling phrases like ‘disaffection’ and scribbling ‘patriotism’ in the margins, his eyes bright, a prison cell door faint behind him.

dialogue.text: Savarkar raided British reports and rebel proclamations for sparks of unity. He stitched scattered risings into a single, deliberate national war against foreign rule.

i18n.hi: सावरकर ने अंग्रेज़ी रिपोर्टों और बाग़ी एलानों में एकता की चिंगारियाँ खोजीं। उसने बिखरे उठावों को जोड़कर विदेशी राज के ख़िलाफ़ एक सोची-समझी राष्ट्रीय जंग बना दिया।

panels.shot: dramatic wide shot of Savarkar before an imagined gathering of 1857 leaders
panels.action: Savarkar stands on an abstract stage, behind him spectral figures of Nana Saheb, Rani Lakshmibai and Kunwar Singh in heroic poses, as if united in council.

dialogue.text: His banned 1909 book turned scattered chiefs and sepoys into pioneers of independence. Many local grievances became, in his telling, conscious steps in a single national plan.

i18n.hi: उसकी १९०९ की प्रतिबंधित किताब ने टुकड़े-टुकड़े सरदारों और सिपाहियों को आज़ादी के अगुवा बना दिया। कई स्थानीय शिकायतें, उसकी कहानी में, एक ही राष्ट्रीय योजना के सोच-समझकर उठाए क़दम बन गईं।

panels.shot: medium shot of Savarkar handing his manuscript to a young Indian activist while a British censor’s hand looms
panels.action: Savarkar passes a manuscript to a young activist in a dim London room, even as an unseen British official’s hand reaches toward a stamping pad marked ‘Prohibited’.

dialogue.text: The British banned his book, fearing its fire. Yet its title—‘First War of Independence’—spread in India, reshaping how a new generation named 1857.

i18n.hi: अंग्रेज़ों ने किताब पर प्रतिबंध लगाया, उसकी आग से डरे। पर उसका नाम—‘फ़र्स्ट वॉर ऑफ़ इंडिपेन्डेन्स’—भारत में फैल गया, और नई पीढ़ी ने १८५७ को नए नाम से देखना शुरू किया।

panels.shot: transition shot: Savarkar’s fiery pamphlet dissolves into neat government files on a 1950s desk
panels.action: Savarkar’s worn pamphlet fades into a tidy stack of government files stamped ‘Centenary 1957’ as Sen’s figure in the Archive Quartet sits down at a modern wooden desk.

dialogue.text: Independence came. By the centenary, the Indian state wanted its own history of 1857—respecting the revolt, yet wary of romantic exaggeration.

i18n.hi: आज़ादी आ गई। सौ बरस पर, भारतीय राज्य को १८५७ की अपनी कहानी चाहिए थी—विद्रोह का सम्मान, पर बेवजह रोमानी बढ़ाचढ़ा से भी दूरी।

panels.shot: medium shot of Sen consulting both Kaye’s and Savarkar’s books alongside archival files
panels.action: Sen sits between Kaye’s thick volumes and Savarkar’s slim book, leafing through yellowed rebel proclamations and administrative papers from the National Archives of India.

dialogue.text: S.N. Sen’s ‘Eighteen Fifty-Seven’ weighed colonial and nationalist accounts against newly opened archives. He honoured resistance, but rejected easy unity and simple labels.

i18n.hi: एस.एन. सेन की ‘एटीन फ़िफ़्टी-सेवन’ ने औपनिवेशिक और राष्ट्रवादी लेखों को नए खुले काग़ज़ों के साथ तौला। उसने प्रतिरोध को सलाम किया, पर आसान एकता और हल्के लेबलों को ठुकराया।

panels.shot: close-up on Sen’s hand making careful notes: ‘local causes’, ‘greed’, ‘grievances’, ‘faith’
panels.action: Sen’s hand writes in a notebook: ‘pay arrears, land revenue, annexation, religious fears’, linking them with arrows rather than one bold slogan.

dialogue.text: Sen showed many causes. Sepoy anger over cartridges, landlords losing estates, princes fearing annexation, religious anxieties—all tangled into one vast upheaval.

i18n.hi: सेन ने कई वजहें दिखाईं। कारतूसों पर सिपाहियों का ग़ुस्सा, ज़मींदारों की ज़मीनें छिनना, राजाओं को राज ख़त्म होने का डर, मज़हबी बेचैनी—सब मिलकर एक बड़ी हलचल बने।

panels.shot: wide shot of Sen addressing an academic audience, with a backdrop map of India marked with local revolts
panels.action: Sen speaks at a lectern, behind him a map of India dotted with small lights marking different centres of revolt, each labelled with local leaders.

dialogue.text: His government-sponsored book balanced pride with caution. 1857 was called ‘a great revolt’, sometimes ‘national in character’, yet not formally declared the single ‘First War’.

i18n.hi: उसकी सरकारी किताब ने गर्व और सावधानी का संतुलन रखा। १८५७ को ‘महान विद्रोह’ कहा गया, कभी ‘राष्ट्रीय रूप वाला’, पर इसे साफ़-साफ़ एक ही ‘फ़र्स्ट वॉर’ नहीं ठहराया गया।

panels.shot: stylised montage: Kaye, Savarkar and Sen fade to the background as Guha steps forward with slim Subaltern Studies volumes
panels.action: The earlier three figures recede into sepia while Guha steps forward, holding thin blue volumes titled with simple ‘Subaltern Studies’, a village scene glowing behind him.

dialogue.text: Then, in the 1980s, another challenge came—not from princes or parliaments, but from the study of peasants, labourers and low-status rebels.

i18n.hi: फिर १९८० के दशक में एक नया चैलेंज आया—राजाओं या संसदों से नहीं, बल्कि किसानों, मज़दूरों और निचले दर्जे के बाग़ियों के अध्ययन से।

panels.shot: close-up on Guha reading an 1857 police report, lines about ‘insurgent rabble’ highlighted
panels.action: Guha sits under a reading lamp, examining a brittle police report from 1857 with phrases like ‘insurgent rabble’ and ‘criminal elements’ carefully underlined.

dialogue.text: Ranajit Guha called colonial writing ‘the prose of counter-insurgency’. He showed how official narratives turned rebels into mere disorder, denying their thought and purpose.

i18n.hi: रणजीत गुहा ने हुकूमती लिखाई को ‘काउंटर इन्सर्जेन्सी की गद्य’ कहा। उसने दिखाया कि कैसे सरकारी कहानी बाग़ियों को सिर्फ़ फ़साद बताती है, उनकी सोच और मुराद छीन लेती है।

panels.shot: medium shot of Guha writing, with ghostly images of peasants and artisans filling the room
panels.action: As Guha writes, translucent figures of peasants with tools, artisans at looms, and village headmen with petitions appear around him, facing the viewer for the first time.

dialogue.text: Subaltern historians asked: where are the villagers, the artisans, the low-ranking soldiers? They were in the records—but only as suspects, defendants, dead men listed by others.

i18n.hi: सबाल्टर्न इतिहासकारों ने पूछा: गाँववाले कहाँ हैं, कारीगर कहाँ हैं, छोटे सिपाही कहाँ हैं? रिकॉर्ड में तो थे—पर सिर्फ़ मुज़रिम, मुलज़िम, या दूसरों की लिखी क़ायदे की लाशों में।

panels.shot: focused shot on Gautam Bhadra within the quartet, studying trial proceedings of obscure rebels
panels.action: Another figure of the Quartet, resembling Gautam Bhadra, bends over trial proceedings, the names of four little-known rebels glowing softly on the page.

dialogue.text: Gautam Bhadra traced four obscure rebels through hostile court records. Piece by piece, he recovered their choices—small acts of defiance that never reached imperial histories.

i18n.hi: गौतम भद्र ने चार गुमनाम बाग़ियों को दुश्मन अदालत की फ़ाइलों से खोजा। टुकड़ा-टुकड़ा जोड़कर उसने उनके फ़ैसले दिखाए—छोटी लेकिन जिद्दी सरकशियाँ, जो कभी साम्राज्य की कहानियों तक पहुँची ही नहीं।

panels.shot: wide shot showing all four historians in a circle, surrounded by maps, proclamations, trial records, and modern books
panels.action: Kaye, Savarkar, Sen and Guha sit facing different directions around one large table piled with maps, proclamations, trial files and recent monographs by Wagner and Dalrymple.

dialogue.text: Modern historians add still more layers—local studies, careful source criticism, new regional archives. No single label—mutiny, war, revolt—can now claim the whole truth.

i18n.hi: आज के इतिहासकार और परतें जोड़ते हैं—स्थानीय पढ़ाई, स्रोतों की बारीक पड़ताल, नए प्रांतीय संग्रह। अब कोई एक नाम—म्यूटिनी, जंग, विद्रोह—पूरी सच्चाई पर दावा नहीं कर सकता।

panels.shot: slow pull-back from the Quartet as 1857 scenes form a vast mosaic on the floor beneath them
panels.action: The camera rises above the Quartet, revealing that they sit atop a huge mosaic of 1857: cantonments, palaces, bazaars, villages, each tile glowing differently under their gaze.

dialogue.speaker: kaye_savarkar_sen_and_guha
dialogue.text: The records speak—but each of us teaches them a different language.

i18n.hi: रिकॉर्ड बोलते हैं—पर हम में से हर कोई उन्हें अलग ज़बान सिखाता है।

panels.shot: final contemplative wide shot: the Quartet fades; only the mosaic and a solitary reader remain
panels.action: The four historians fade into silhouettes; a contemporary reader stands alone on the mosaic of 1857, holding a notebook, looking down as if weighing the many images.

dialogue.text: To know 1857 is to read its mutiny, its war, its revolt—and to ask, each time, who is speaking, what they saw, and what they chose not to see.

i18n.hi: १८५७ को जानना है तो उसकी म्यूटिनी, उसकी जंग, उसका विद्रोह सब पढ़ना होगा—और हर बार पूछना होगा: बोल कौन रहा है, उसने क्या देखा, और क्या देखने से इंकार किया।

subtitle_i18n.en: Four Historians, One Uprising, Many Wars Over Memory
subtitle_i18n.hi: चार इतिहासकार, एक बग़ावत, और यादों की अनगिनत जंगें
